name: The Suffolk Coast
notes: Site-wide header newsletter signup (single email field, ASP.NET WebForms postback), distinct from the 'competition-entry-2' prize draw form already tracked as a competition. Org already tracked via the suffolk-coast competition adapter.

name: Visit Essex
notes: Standalone e-newsletter sign-up page, separate from the visit-essex-gardeners-world competition entry form found in the same run. Requires name/email/address fields; the newsletter consent checkbox is this page's sole purpose and is ticked deliberately.

name: Visit North Norfolk
notes: Standalone Mailchimp e-newsletter signup, separate from the north-norfolk-attractions competition entry form found in the same run (different page/engine — this one's Mailchimp, that one's NewMind/eCMS). Requires email + name; the 'Yes, from yourselves' dropdown and GDPR email-channel checkbox are this page's sole purpose and are set deliberately. Org already tracked via the north-norfolk-attractions competition adapter.

name: Coast Magazine
notes: Standalone newsletter signup (dotdigital/Kelsey landing page, different URL from the coast-magazine-suffolk-coast competition's own entry form, though same underlying platform). Requires name/email; opts into 'Beachcomber' (Coast's general newsletter) only, not the separate 'Coast Property' one or the broader 'Kelsey Publishing promotional emails' checkbox. Org already tracked via the coast-magazine-suffolk-coast competition adapter.

name: Devon's Top Attractions
notes: Standalone Mailchimp hosted signup page (linked from a 'Newsletter Sign up' panel on the same page as the devons-top-attractions competition, but a genuinely separate submission — different platform, Mailchimp vs that page's own Gravity Forms). Requires email; name/phone/county optional. Three GDPR contact-channel checkboxes present (Email/Direct Mail/Customized online advertising) — only 'Email' ticked, since that's this newsletter's own delivery channel, not third-party sharing. Org already tracked via the devons-top-attractions competition adapter.

name: Virgin Atlantic Holidays
notes: Official Virgin Atlantic Holidays (virginatlantic.com/holidays, redirects from virginholidays.co.uk) newsletter signup, first-party, no purchase/account necessary. AngularJS form: first name + email only. No genuine open no-purchase-necessary competition found for Virgin Holidays at time of writing (only a paid/Ireland-specific holiday competitions site and unrelated Virgin Money/Virgin Media promos turned up) — newsletter only for now; worth re-checking for a competition later.

name: Emirates
notes: Official Emirates (emirates.com) 'Subscribe to special offers' page, first-party. The page shows a flashy 'STEP 1 OF 2' wizard, but that's a full account/preferences flow — targets the simpler standalone footer widget instead, a genuine <form action="/english/special-offers/subscribe-to-offers/"> with just email + Subscribe. Confirmed directly: the top wizard's own email field and this footer form's share the literal id "email" (a real duplicate-id bug on Emirates' own markup) — every selector is scoped to the footer form specifically to avoid resolving to the wrong one. OneTrust cookie banner; its dark backdrop lingers after the reject click, so the adapter waits for #onetrust-consent-sdk to fully detach before interacting further. No genuine open no-purchase-necessary Emirates Holidays UK competition found at time of writing.

name: Jet2holidays
notes: Official Jet2holidays (jet2holidays.com) email sign-up page, first-party, no purchase/account necessary. Single email field (input[name=email]) + Sign up button (#btn-email), standard OneTrust cookie banner. No genuine open no-purchase-necessary Jet2holidays competition found at time of writing (the ones that turned up in search had already closed). easyJet Holidays checked and skipped: easyjet.com returns a persistent 403 on a plain page load (confirmed twice), not just at submit — genuine bot-protection block, not evaded.

name: Colchester Zoo
notes: Colchester Zoo (Colchester Zoological Society), Essex — genuine Mailchimp hosted signup page, linked from the zoo's own official site. First name, last name, and email all required by this form (verified directly against each field's own 'This field is required' text). GDPR contact-channel checkboxes (Email/Direct Mail) present — only 'Email' ticked, same as devons-top-attractions-newsletter. No currently open first-party competition found on the zoo's own domain (past ones ran via Facebook or third-party blogs, not a web form) — newsletter only. Uses the same list-manage.com hosted-subscribe-page pattern already documented as connection-blocked for devons-top-attractions-newsletter (different Mailchimp shard, us18 vs us9, so worth checking directly rather than assuming the same result).

name: Adventure Island
notes: Adventure Island, Southend-on-Sea's own theme park (adventureisland.co.uk) — genuine first-party newsletter, a simple Elementor Pro footer form on the homepage (optional Name + required Email). CookieYes cookie banner (.cky-btn-reject). No currently open no-purchase-necessary competition found on this org's own domain at time of writing (a past c2c-run Adventure Island annual-pass giveaway on c2c-online.co.uk, already tracked separately via c2c-blowout-company, is stale/closed from 2024) — newsletter only.

name: Visit Lake District
notes: Official Visit Lake District (run by Cumbria Tourism) newsletter, standard Mailchimp classic embed. Required: Email, First Name, Last Name, Country of residence (UK selected). Optional: Title, Postcode, a 'What holiday interests you?' checkbox group (left untouched). Only the organiser's own GDPR consent checkbox is ticked. Org already tracked via the visit-lake-district-prize-draw competition adapter.

name: Solmar Villas
notes: Official Solmar Villas (solmarvillas.com) homepage newsletter signup, a genuine Drupal Webform ('Sign up today for exclusive offers'), separate from the British Travel Awards vote-to-win competition already tracked via solmar-villas-british-travel-awards (different site, britishtravelawards.com). First name, last name, email. Confirmed directly from the served HTML: this form always renders a visible reCAPTCHA v2 image challenge (data-type="image", not conditional) — adapter fills the form and fails loudly at that point rather than solving/evading it, same category as c2c-blowout-company and visit-essex-gardeners-world (submit-time reCAPTCHA, not a page-load block). Worth re-checking if Solmar ever drops the reCAPTCHA from this form.

name: Visit Colchester
notes: Colchester City Council's own tourism newsletter ('What's On from Visit Colchester'), linked from visitcolchester.com's footer — genuinely distinct org from the already-tracked colchester-zoo-newsletter (council tourism board vs. the zoo itself). Standalone e-shot.net (Wired Plus) landing page, fully static HTML (verified via curl): single required email field, a text honeypot ('website', visually offscreen not type=hidden, left untouched), and a 'CapToken' hidden field wired to a silent proof-of-work anti-bot widget (cap.e-shot.net) expected to self-populate on page load — adapter waits for it and fails loudly (not solved/evaded) if it never populates. List is DoubleOptIn, so a successful submit here just triggers Colchester's own confirmation email. AJAX form swap, success read from real wording. Same sandbox-networking caveat as other adapters this run (curl-verified only) — first live run worth a human's eyes, especially the CapToken behaviour.

name: Fred. Olsen Cruise Lines
notes: Official first-party homepage footer newsletter signup, first UK cruise line tried in this project (P&O Cruises and Cunard/MSC already excluded as bot-protected). Custom-built form (First_Name/Last_Name/Email) posting to /focl-email-signup/submit-email-signup, verified directly against the real served HTML (unquoted-attribute markup, e.g. name=First_Name — confirmed selectors still resolve fine, a grep quoting quirk during review, not a real issue). Honeypot field 'field1P0t' left blank. An 'ondemand' reCAPTCHA div is present but per its own naming should only render on suspicious signals rather than unconditionally — adapter checks and fails loudly if it ever appears. OneTrust cookie banner. No client-visible confirmation text found in the static HTML — treats HTTP OK with no visible error as success, same convention as suffolkCoast.ts. No open no-purchase competition found on this domain (/competition redirects to the homepage).

name: Saga Cruises
notes: Official first-party newsletter banner (Saga Cruises Limited, the over-50s specialist), no purchase/account necessary. Clean ASP.NET MVC form (#email-only-form -> POST /emailonly/banner): First Name, Last Name, Email only, no marketing checkbox to leave unticked. Known real failure copy ('unable to subscribe you at this time') checked in both the POST response body and the DOM; anything else treated as success. Saga's genuine no-purchase cruise prize draws (e.g. 'Win a river cruise', 50+ only) were NOT built — they require a JS-driven postcode/address-lookup widget whose manual-entry fields don't exist in static HTML, plus consent-checkbox markup injected by further unknown JS — real selectors this project has no way to discover without live JS rendering; deliberately not guessed. Worth a future adapter attempt in an environment with working Playwright access, checking profile.dateOfBirth against the 50+ age restriction (SKIPPED_RULES, not FAILED, if too young or DOB unset) before reaching the address-widget problem.

name: Toad Hall Cottages
notes: Cornwall/Devon/Dorset/Somerset/Exmoor/Dartmoor/New Forest holiday cottage agency, official first-party newsletter form (Title/first name/surname/email required; destination/holiday-type/bedroom preference checkboxes left untouched). Confirmed directly from the served HTML: this form always renders a standard Google reCAPTCHA v2 checkbox widget, unconditionally present (not conditional the way Fred Olsen's 'ondemand' one is). Adapter fills the whole form then fails loudly at the final submit once the challenge is confirmed present, same category as c2c-blowout-company and solmar-villas-newsletter (submit-time reCAPTCHA, not a page-load block). Real confirmation text captured for if/when this is ever resolved: '#postForm' -> 'Thank you for you for signing up, we look forward to emailing you soon.' No competition found on this domain.

name: Classic Cottages
notes: Independent Cornwall-based (Hayle) holiday cottage agency, official first-party footer newsletter, single email field. Client-side AJAX submit toggling real .newsletter__success ('Thank you — Keep an eye out for our welcome email...') / .newsletter__error ('Sorry, an error has occurred... please call us on 01326 555555') panels, both wordings confirmed directly from the served HTML. CookieYes banner, same .cky-btn-reject selector already used by adventure-island-newsletter. No first-party competition found on classic.co.uk — the '£250/£500 Classic Cottages voucher' prizes found are run by third parties (The Good Web Guide, olive magazine) as their own promotions with Classic Cottages product as the prize, not entered on Classic Cottages' own site.

name: Anchor Bay Holidays
notes: Official UK holiday cottage agency, first-party Sendinblue/Brevo embedded newsletter form (First Name, Last Name, Email). This page's own '£500 Voucher Competition' already closed for 2026 (a winner was announced) — but per the page's own text, every active subscriber is automatically entered into next year's draw, so the newsletter itself is worth having regardless. Invisible reCAPTCHA v2 badge present (confirmed no visible challenge box) — checked for a rendered visible challenge right before submit and fails loudly if one appears, not assumed blocking just because the badge exists.

name: Marie Claire
notes: Marie Claire's own first-party newsletter signup, distinct from any of the already-tracked comps.marieclaire.co.uk daily prize-draw entries (dmri-comps adapter, different subdomain/platform). Uses Future PLC's shared 'newsletterForm' widget — a real form hydrated from a JSON config embedded directly in the page (read directly from the raw HTML, not guessed): single required email field (name=MAIL), two independently-optional checkboxes for 'other Future brands' and 'trusted partners or sponsors' marketing left unticked, submits as 'Sign me up'. Confirmed the identical widget/config also renders on womanandhome.com/newsletter (same publisher, different brand) — adapterKey (future-plc-newsletter) is written generically against the shared widget rather than hardcoded to Marie Claire, so any other Future PLC title's newsletter can reuse it later via a new row here rather than a new adapter file. Same Sourcepoint consent-management iframe (privacy-mgmt.com) already documented on this publisher's comps.* subdomains in dmriComps.ts, dismissed the same way (Agree — no one-click reject-all offered).

name: Ambassador Cruise Line
notes: Ambassador Cruise Line's own mailing-list signup, separate from the already-tracked ambassador-cruise-line-england-golf competition on the same site. Vue/Nuxt page with custom Radix Vue widgets (hidden native inputs behind styled buttons/labels) — verified via curl (server-rendered, not a client-only SPA shell). Required: first name, surname, email, and a single checkbox that IS the newsletter opt-in ('I have read the privacy policy and would like to receive news and offers to my inbox') — ticked here since this is the newsletter adapter, not the competition one. Region/age-range/postal-comms preference left at their sensible defaults (all optional, no matching profile field). Could not verify a live post-submit confirmation string or any cookie-consent banner during this research pass (this session's headless-browser tooling couldn't reach the live site — static HTML only), so the adapter matches confirmation text broadly by wording; worth double-checking against a real dry run once the local runner has live browser access.

name: Woman & Home
notes: Second Future PLC title confirmed on the shared 'newsletterForm' widget that futurePlcNewsletter.ts was deliberately written generically against — this exact URL was already identified as compatible when that adapter was built (see its own docblock) but never actually registered as a row until now. Re-verified directly this run: HTTP 200 (note the page 301s from the bare /newsletter to /newsletter/ — use the trailing-slash URL directly), real served HTML contains the same slice-container-newsletterForm widget and input[name=MAIL] as marieclaire.co.uk/newsletter. No code changes needed, same adapterKey.

name: Diggerland UK
notes: First-party newsletter, org already tracked via the diggerland-prize-draw competition adapter but a genuinely separate page/form. Self-hosted Sendy form (posts to diggerland.ovh/sendy/subscribe) with name/email and a GDPR marketing-consent checkbox that IS this newsletter's own opt-in (ticked here, unlike a competition form's marketing checkbox). Text honeypot field (#hp, hidden via a wrapping display:none div) left blank. No reCAPTCHA present on this specific form's markup (the site bundles a Contact Form 7 reCAPTCHA plugin site-wide, already documented on the prize-draw adapter as scoped elsewhere) — adapter checks for one at submit and fails loudly if it ever appears rather than solving it. This is a plain cross-origin form POST, not AJAX, so a successful submit navigates the browser to diggerland.ovh and the response body is Sendy's own small, stable, tool-hardcoded plain-text output (confirmed via Sendy's own documentation/forum, not guessed) — '1' for a fresh subscribe, 'Already subscribed.', a 'confirm your email' message for double opt-in, or an 'Error: ...' string — matched directly in the adapter rather than assuming HTTP 200 means success.

name: GoodTo
notes: Third Future PLC title on the same shared newsletterForm widget as Marie Claire and Woman & Home — GoodTo (Future PLC's family/parenting/lifestyle title; womansweekly.com itself now redirects here, so this is also effectively Woman's Weekly's current newsletter home). Re-verified directly: HTTP 200, real served HTML contains input[name=MAIL] and the widget's own embedded success copy ('Thank you for signing up. You will receive a confirmation email shortly.') and failure copy ('There was a problem. Please refresh the page and try again.') matching what futurePlcNewsletter.ts already expects — no code changes needed, same adapterKey. Note: www.woman.co.uk (the separate 'Woman' magazine title) returned a clean HTTP 403 with a StackPath-style bot-protection header (x-stackprotect-id) on a plain page-load fetch, not a sandbox networking artifact (that failure mode here has always been a connection reset, not a clean 403) — treating that one as a genuine page-load bot block and not pursuing it further for now.

name: Away Resorts
notes: Official Away Resorts (awayresorts.co.uk, ~20 UK holiday parks including Mersea Island, Essex — genuinely local to this profile) 'Sign up to Latest Offers' newsletter, first-party, no purchase/account necessary. Real form (#brochure-form-offers-signup, POST /api/form/, EnquiryType=Newsletter) confirmed directly from served HTML: Title/first/last name/email required, phone optional, a required 'How did you hear about us?' dropdown answered 'Search Engine' (genuinely how this project found the page), and ~20 optional park-interest checkboxes left untouched (content preference, not marketing consent — the form's whole purpose is the newsletter itself, no separate opt-in checkbox exists). This form always renders a visible (non-invisible) reCAPTCHA v2 checkbox widget — adapter fills the form and fails loudly at that point rather than solving/evading it, same category as c2c-blowout-company and solmar-villas-newsletter. No live competition currently found on Away Resorts' own site (past 'Beach Holiday Giveaway 2026' closed 30 June 2026; a 'Selfies' page is a subjective photo competition, excluded as needing fabricated creative content) — newsletter only for now. Same egress-proxy sandbox limitation as other entries in this file confirmed this session (curl-verified server-rendered HTML only, no live Playwright render) — also directly confirmed this run that greatrail.com and parkdeanresorts.co.uk are both behind a page-load-blocking Cloudflare challenge (skip, not evaded) and that eurocamp.co.uk's newsletter signup is a client-rendered Next.js page with no real form markup in the static HTML — not built, real field names couldn't be confirmed without a working live browser render.
